summary: PICSP3D is an open-source, three-dimensional, three-velocity (3D3V) electrostatic particle-in-cell code for plasma-object interaction, such as spacecraft and probe charging, sheaths and wakes, Langmuir probes, dust grains, electrodes, magnetised plasma devices and gas discharges. Objects of arbitrary shape are embedded in a uniform Cartesian grid as signed distance functions, built from analytic primitives with constructive solid geometry or imported from CAD (STL) with generalised winding numbers. The Poisson equation is solved with a multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradient method and second-order Shortley-Weller cut cells; floating and biased conductors are charged self-consistently through a capacitance matrix. The code includes surface processes (absorption, secondary electron emission, photoemission with self-shadowing), uniform and spatially varying static magnetic fields (dipoles, current loops, solenoids, mirrors, wires) with a Boris pusher, Monte Carlo collisions with a neutral background (elastic, charge exchange, excitation, ionisation) and binary Coulomb collisions. The solver is written in C++20 and parallelised with MPI domain decomposition and OpenMP threads; output is parallel VTK. A Python package, picsp_post, provides post-processing, figures, animations, Blender renders and a CAD import tool. The release contains the test suite, sixteen documented example cases with analysis scripts, the scaling benchmark and its results. Figures (in the repository): Logo ; CubeSat in low Earth orbit ; CubeSat ion wake ; protons trapped in a dipole field ; floating sphere and OML theory ; two-stream instability ; strong scaling on 72 cores . The full gallery and documentation are in the README .

Bayesian Inference Pipeline : Reconstructs full-resolution reflectance spectra with uncertainty bounds ($1\sigma$ and $90%$ credible intervals) from broadband magnitude colors (e.g., LSST or DES). Photometric & Reverse Projection Utilities : Tools to sample latent distributions and project them back into synthetic optical color spaces. Contents & Structure src/ : Core Python modules for spectral reconstruction, GMM sampling, reverse projection, and photometric flux conversions. models/ : Pre-trained PCA/KDE models and AutoGluon reconstructor configurations. .agents/skills/spectra_reconstruction/ : CLI scripts and automated agent skill definitions. summary: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices. PlantVLM-Edge combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and on-device serving with an offline chat interface, allowing growers to ask open-ended questions and receive diagnoses, symptom explanations, and management guidance without cloud connectivity. The framework is backbone-agnostic: we validate it with two different VLM types with varying scale and architecture (Qwen3-VL-2B and LLaVA-1.5-7B), four quantization schemes, and two diagnostic domains (plant diseases and insect pests), and we deploy all variants on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Eight-bit quantization affects answer quality minimally relative to the full-precision model, and 4-bit activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ) retains 98.6% of full-precision answer quality on both domains while reducing the weight memory of the 2B backbone by 49%. In its most compact form, PlantVLM-Edge requires 2.01 GiB of weight memory, returns its first token in about 0.12 s, and completes a 64-token diagnostic response in 0.78 s. These results demonstrate that timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is practical on edge devices, providing a foundation for next-generation crop monitoring and decision support systems.
title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis

summary: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.
title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference

summary: The term "AI slop" is commonly treated as a property of the generator: text is slop because a model produced it. This paper argues that slop is a property of the process. It names generation that reached a reader without the review it needed, and reviewed generation is a draft, whoever generated it. On that account the slop critique is largely mitigable by review processes run with or by language models, but not on the grounds usually offered. The argument is not that models review better than they write, nor that they review better than humans. It is that one large class of faults, provenance, is invisible to a reading human at population scale and cheap for a machine to check: across four top-tier venues, papers carrying hallucinated citations received reviewer ratings indistinguishable from clean papers, accepted and rejected submissions whose ratings differed by two points carried the same share of them, and a venue-scale audit cost about four cents a paper (Russinovich, Siva Kumar and Salem 2026). Review is the better-suited task for a model for five structural reasons: a fixed target, a brief that says where to look, permission to answer "cannot verify", no stake in the document, and the generated text as a map of where to check. The remedy for slop is therefore a division of labour that assigns the provenance pass to the machine and the reasoning pass to the human. The paper names five mechanisms by which unreviewed generation acquires faults that are invisible from inside the text, carries four corrections as explicit limits, and reports one case in which two reviewers of different kind, a human on a phone and a model under a provenance brief, found disjoint error classes with no overlap, every provenance fault sitting on a source the generating model had not opened. The case is N = 1 and is offered as a specimen, not a result; the paper's own first draft supplies a second specimen, by the mechanism the paper describes. The division of labour is then placed under its binding constraint: when an AI agent is institutionally positioned as an employee, managers catch fewer errors themselves and pass the review on (Wiles, Hsu, Bedard and Kropp 2026), so the design must survive the effect it is meant to offset. Seven hypotheses are stated, each with the observation that would falsify it.
title: Slop Is a Process Property

summary: Sensor fusion, data fusion, dashboards and data visualisation are conventionally distinguished by input type and by where they sit in a processing stack. This paper argues that the distinction which matters for decision quality is a different one, and that it is two variables applied to all four: every representation of multi-source evidence collapses a distribution somewhere between sensor and decision, and representations differ in the locus of that collapse and in whether the residual uncertainty survives it as a carried object. Fusion collapses upstream and, when honest, ships the residual as covariance or hypothesis mass. Dashboards defer collapse to the viewer's retina and ship nothing; the resulting belief has no bookkeeping. Visualisation is the encoding of whichever object arrives, indifferent to whether it is a point or a distribution, which is why it is blamed for collapses committed upstream. The two variables, collapse locus and residual retention, place the four terms on one map, generalise the confabulation coefficient of The Confabulating Collator from language-model collators to the whole representation stack, and yield a diagnostic: the failure mode conventionally called bad fusion is a product that collapsed upstream and discarded its residual, delivering the confidence of a posterior with the epistemic hygiene of a gauge. The publicly reported expectation, in the investigation of the February 2026 Minab strike, that a targeting platform would have flagged contradictions it carried no representation of, is read as this failure at operational scale, with the causal question left where the public record leaves it. A design rule follows: defer collapse to the human where the human carries the prior the system lacks, fuse where they do not, and at neither locus discard the residual. The constructive requirement for language-level fusion products is stated and handed to a companion paper on divergence retention. The operator located in the architecture is Binary Bias.
title: Where the Cloud Collapses

summary: Binary Bias (Temte 2026a) claims that the collapse of continuous, conditional and multi-valued phenomena into sealed either/or categories is a substrate from which other catalogued biases grow. The claim has so far been argued, not counted. This paper specifies an audit that counts it: a random sample of 3,000 journal-article abstracts drawn through Crossref's sampling endpoint, enriched with field and era metadata from OpenAlex, and coded for binary collapse by three independent language-model coders with ten percent human double-coding. The coding scheme separates four loci at which a binary can sit (territory, design, inference, format), scores severity on a 0 to 5 Boolikert rather than as present or absent, and counts the sealing of a null result into an absence claim (nulsegl) as its own category. An evening-scale pilot of twenty abstracts, reported in full, motivates six hypotheses with pre-stated effect sizes: that inference- and format-locus collapse appears in at least a quarter of abstracts; that the format locus dominates in clinical literature and the inference locus in social and policy literature; that nulsegl is the single most frequent collapse type; that fields whose core object is already a ratio collapse less than fields whose core object is a category; that the 2016 statement on p-values changed vocabulary rather than verdicts; and that abstracts collapse more than the discussion sections they summarise. Publication of the protocol before the data is the pre-registration; the result is published whichever way it falls.
title: Counting the Collapse

summary: Validation dataset of the H5MD biophysics module, a metadata schema that stores the topology, force field, MD parameters, selection groups and observables of a molecular dynamics simulation together with its trajectory in one H5MD (HDF5) file. It accompanies the paper A Hierarchical Metadata Schema for Self-Contained Molecular Dynamics Trajectory Archives . validation_systems.zip contains the GROMACS inputs of the 58 chemical systems used in the paper's technical validation, reduced to what grompp needs: topology, force field, coordinates or run input, index groups and MD parameters. The systems range from 711 to 1,066,628 particles, cover AMBER, CHARMM, GROMOS, OPLS-AA and MARTINI force fields, and come in six groups by origin: self_generated (8): built with GROMACS from PDB entries bena (10): sessions of the Bena dataset ( 10.5281/zenodo.17632513 ) jcp_benchmark (6): GROMACS benchmark systems ( 10.5281/zenodo.3893789 ) hexabc (8): hexABC nucleic-acid and protein–nucleic-acid deposits from MDposit memprotmd (6): MemProtMD membrane proteins, atomistic and coarse-grained misato (20): MISATO protein–ligand complexes ( 10.5281/zenodo.7711953 ) Run under 23 simulation protocols, these inputs give the 379 reference files of the validation. The files can be regenerated with the validation scripts ( github.com/miemiemmmm/h5md-biophysics-validation ) and the GROMACS implementation published with the paper. Each group's MANIFEST.md credits its source and states the changes made; provenance/ holds the scripts that selected and prepared the systems. Four of the reference files are included as examples, each a short trajectory with the full metadata. They also serve as test data for the validator in gitlab.com/gromacs/h5md-biophysics : hexabc_a001u2_rna_protein__nvt-vrescale.h5md bench_villin__tcoupl-multigroup.h5md bench_villin__sd-langevin.h5md bench_villin__selection-noncontiguous.h5md
title: Validation systems and reference files for the H5MD biophysics metadata module

summary: A shibboleth economy is a cultural system in which the rewards of decoding, a fluency-gain reward, identity affirmation, collective affiliation, and positional rank, become self-sustaining, so that demand for distinction feeds back into cultural production and communicative opacity becomes value-bearing rather than merely costly. Cultural capital theory, from Bourdieu through the fan-studies lineage, explains why scarce decoding competence produces distinction; a shibboleth economy begins where that distinction becomes demand and the demand alters what gets made, through evolutionary selection on engagement rather than any calculating producer. The paper develops the loop and its consequences. A two-type model distinguishes lexical figuration, which maps represented features to meanings and is bootstrappable within a single work, from modal figuration, which maps the representational act itself to an ontological status and is stabilised only by shared representational infrastructure, of which canon is the most powerful form. In markets poor in effective codebook coverage, exemplified by industrial-era Hollywood, uncaught references are priced as lost customers and a self-teaching visual pidgin is selected, later mistaken for neutral realism; in codebook-rich markets the operating point moves to selective permeability, legible to the invested and closed to the casual, with the equilibrium set by the opposed pulls of affiliation and rank. Democratisation of a key causes migration and displacement rather than collapse; a hard cultural border is a boundary condition that slows depreciation and opens an export axis; and when demand for keys outruns authenticated supply, the predicted pathology is key inflation, defined as growth in the ratio of claimed authorised readings to verifiably authorised ones, driven by provenance laundering. Two model-implied expectations, codebook import markets and synthetic canon manufacture, are tested against known cases, with modal transfer breadth as the surviving strong claim, and three forward predictions are stated, led by key migration under democratisation.
title: The Shibboleth Economy

summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) tackle challenging tasks by dividing work among agents and coordinating their contributions toward shared objectives. Evaluating these systems therefore requires benchmarks that assess not only task-solving performance but also the ability to handle interdependent work. However, existing benchmarks often emphasize task difficulty without substantial collaboration requirements or evaluate only a limited range of predefined collaboration patterns. In this paper, we introduce MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration through interconnected tasks. Rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols, MAC-Bench embeds collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints. Specifically, we mine reusable collaboration structures from selected benchmark tasks at two levels. Local collaboration patterns capture recurring interactions among subtasks, while global task structures characterize how these interactions contribute to complete workflows. Through coarse-to-fine composition, these structures are recombined into task graphs combining different collaboration requirements. Tasks are instantiated in executable environments with automated verification of partial progress and complete task resolution.
title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks

summary: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.
title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations

summary: Abstract: Keeping the modern power grid running during heatwaves, wildfires, or cyberattacks requires knowing which power lines are the most dangerous "dominoes" if two or three of them fail at the same time. However, checking every possible combination of multiple broken lines across the Western U.S. grid is a math problem with millions of possibilities—far too slow for computers to solve in real time using standard physics equations. Conversely, taking shortcuts by simply looking at a map of the grid (to find the biggest, most connected hubs) fails because electricity does not travel like cars on a highway; it cannot be told which road to take. Instead, electricity automatically splits across all available wires based on their physical resistance. When a major line gets crowded or breaks, electricity surges onto smaller side-lines, causing chain-reaction blackouts far away from the original problem. In this memo, we introduce Physics-Informed Network Reshaping (PINR), an AI framework that bridges the gap between map-based speed and physical accuracy. PINR combines a specialized, mathematically predictable neural network with a network-disruption algorithm originally designed for counter-terrorism. Rather than testing millions of broken-wire combinations one by one, PINR uses a single, rapid pass to act as a dual-use stress gauge: For Grid Defenders ("Blue Team" Healing): It shows grid operators the exact 27 congested power lines where slightly "throttling" the flow (like adjusting valves on a water pipe) relieves 99.1% of grid overloads during a peak evening crunch, pushing excess electricity safely onto underused backup lines. For Security Analysts ("Red Team" Vulnerability Hunting): Because the lines that need the most throttling to heal the grid are the exact same lines carrying the most dangerous physical stress, PINR automatically narrows the search for catastrophic multi-line failures from 235 lines down to just 27. This cuts the number of three-line failure combinations to check by 99.86% (from over 2.1 million down to under 3,000). Most importantly, testing PINR on the 2026 Western Energy Imbalance Market (WEIM) proves that looking at a static map of the grid is dangerously misleading. While standard map-based analysis points to California's central grid hub (CAISO) as the most critical choke point, PINR's physics engine reveals that California's many parallel lines easily absorb the load. Instead, the true physical bottlenecks hide in the power-exporting corridors of the Desert Southwest (Arizona and the Lower Colorado River) and the mountain seams connecting Montana, the Pacific Northwest, and Utah. Correspondence and collaboration inquiries: aes@acm.org
title: Physics-Informed Network Reshaping (PINR) for Western Grid Resilience

summary: This repository presents an evidence-anchored, discipline-sensitive multicriteria assessment framework designed to support transparent, accountable, and reproducible evaluations of academic distinction and research integrity. The framework comprises a Microsoft Excel workbook organized into seven disciplinary classes corresponding to those of the European Academy of Sciences and Arts (EASA): 1. Humanities 2. Medicine 3. Arts 4. Natural Sciences 5. Social Sciences 6. Environmental and Technical Sciences 7. World Religions Each disciplinary class includes ten weighted assessment criteria evaluated on a five-level ordinal scale (0–4). Weighted scores are aggregated and normalized against the maximum attainable score for each class, generating percentage-based results and illustrative classification guidance. The workbook contains 15 worksheets, including discipline-specific evaluation forms, a scoring protocol, research integrity resources, an integrity register, a reusable audit template, and guidance for nominators. A central feature of the framework is the separation of academic merit assessment from research integrity verification. The integrity workflow supports the documentation and contextual examination of retractions, expressions of concern, citation irregularities, potential publication anomalies, and editorial or peer-review conflicts of interest. The framework distinguishes between unverified allegations, documented concerns, and substantiated findings. Bibliometric anomalies, retractions, or incomplete verification procedures must not automatically be interpreted as proof of individual research misconduct. The workbook also incorporates guidance for nominators regarding documentary evidence and the distinction between achievements that are not documented, criteria that have not yet been assessed, and verified absence of specific achievements. The assessment framework is intended to facilitate structured scholarly judgment rather than replace it. Its numerical weights and classification thresholds are illustrative methodological parameters and have not undergone independent empirical validation. Scope and limitations The instrument is proposed for academic discussion, methodological evaluation, pilot testing, and potential institutional adaptation. It is not an autonomous research misconduct detection system or a validated psychometric instrument. The workbook does not independently retrieve or verify bibliometric information. External sources require manual verification or separately implemented data-population procedures. The framework was independently developed with reference to the seven disciplinary classes of EASA. It does not constitute an officially adopted assessment policy of the European Academy of Sciences and Arts (EASA) or the World Academy of Art and Science (WAAS). Reproducibility and responsible use The accompanying README provides methodological information, scoring instructions, evidence requirements, research integrity safeguards, and limitations. Users are encouraged to document the evidence supporting individual scores, distinguish missing information from verified negative findings, and ensure independent review and appropriate procedural fairness before making consequential decisions. This Version 1.0 is provided as a transparent and reusable methodological resource for further examination, testing, and refinement. Keywords : Academic Evaluation; Research Integrity; Multicriteria Decision Analysis; Responsible Research Assessment; Evidence-Based Assessment; Bibliometrics; Academic Governance; Research Integrity Auditing; Academic Nominations; Scholarly Excellence.

title: Evidence-Anchored Multicriteria Assessment and Research Integrity: A Seven-Class Evaluation Workbook

summary: This deposit is the archived version of record for BioFirewall v0.2.0, a defensive, design-stage screen for agentic genome-writing AI. BioFirewall intercepts a genome-writing plan in workflow, and returns allow , flag-for-review or refuse across five hazard axes native to genome writing (cargo, locus, edit type, germline and scale), with cited evidence, a calibrated false-refuse ceiling, a competence-conditioned confidence, an HMAC-signed design passport, a hash-chained audit log and a tiered managed-access plane. Contents: the complete source snapshot at the v0.2.0 tag; the open hazard data the five axes read (embedding centroids, oncogene and tumour-suppressor annotation, dosage-constraint and essentiality scores, curated fusion knowledge); the frozen benchmark, red-team and language-model panel results, including the reported negatives; the CCGD-derived positive sets and the locus outcome-validation result; five SHA-locked pre-registrations; the documentation set (threat model, hazard taxonomy, benchmark, head-to-head, system card, panel, hazard knowledge base, standards, cloud-lab integration); and the clean-image verification logs. Open data only. It contains no hazard sequences or evasion instructions; hazard signatures are held at the function, family, and taxon levels. The licence-restricted oracles (COSMIC, OncoKB), the cargo sequences and the run artefacts are excluded and are never committed. Every file is listed in SHA256SUMS and verifies with sha256sum -c. Source repository: https://github.com/ahmedanees-m/bio-firewall (tag v0.2.0). Requires PEN-STACK (declared range pen-stack>=0.2.0,<0.3.0). RRID:SCR_028785. bio.tools: biotools:bio-firewall. Licensing: Apache-2.0. Third-party open datasets are referenced at their home repositories under their own terms and are not re-licensed here; see DATA_LICENSES.md.
title: BioFirewall: a rule-governed, genome-writing-native biosecurity middleware that supervises agentic design AI

summary: Measured failure modes of verifier panels: companion paper accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? — Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels . Version of record: SSRN 7390698 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7390698 . Cite that version. The same text is also at https://polyhelper.ai/research/agreement-not-evidence/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/agreement-not-evidence . Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a non-expert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem: reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of "ten of them agreed." The protocol formalized here collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user's own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server. It reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich: the strongest available answer becomes the base, and each of the others contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it. Disagreements are kept in a section of their own rather than averaged away. The paper makes four contributions. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a merge can fail. Four of them are defects of naive pooling; the fifth is a failure of the operator rather than of the method: a synthesis that presents a single model's output as a collegial result. The second is the application of the correlated-witness arithmetic to protocol design. That arithmetic is not claimed here. Kohli (2026) applied the same Kish correction to a panel of nine frontier judges and measured about two effective votes, and Kim et al. (2025) established the underlying error correlation across more than 350 models. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Once a council is larger than 1/ρ, halving ρ beats doubling N, and a pair with low error correlation can outweigh five with high correlation. Which pairs those are is measured, not read off the label: the larger and more accurate models carry the most correlated errors even when architecture and provider differ (Kim et al., 2025), and the author's per-pair measurements found no detectable effect of geopolitical bloc on error correlation and, in the pairs measured, none of shared lineage (Chernets, 2026). The estimation procedure of Section 5.5 supplies that measurement. The third is an account of three deployment tiers, manual, one-tap mobile and browser-agent, and of the axis that separates them epistemically: whether the second model sees the first model's answer. Conditioning the second model raises ρ in exchange for error correction. The fourth is a small-sample observation of the counterfeit-council failure across five models, the one-sentence intervention that removed it in a three-model re-run, and a blinded three-arm evaluation design with a stated falsification condition. Correlated agreement is treated here as established, not as a finding. That a panel of models is worth far fewer independent witnesses than it has members has been measured directly: nine frontier judges drawn from seven families supply about two effective votes (Kohli, 2026), and error correlation rises with model capability even across providers and architectures (Kim et al., 2025). Section 5 restates the design-effect arithmetic behind those measurements, because three of the protocol's rules are derived from it and read as fastidiousness without it. The protocol then takes the other side of the same problem. That literature measures the correlation; this protocol

summary: A provenance-bound values model published as a public evaluator rather than deployed as a filter — why open weights defeat a filter and strengthen a referee, why the same weights bear three different relations to the model they judge, and why an evaluator that gatekeeps its own judgments has reproduced the defect it exists to correct. A values model — a model that judges conduct against a standard — is an established artifact. Guard models, safety classifiers, critic models, preference models and process reward models all instantiate the family, and the engineering is not in dispute. What is in dispute, and what this paper specifies, is the posture in which such an artifact is published , which we argue is not a deployment detail but the property that determines whether the artifact does anything at all. We state an inversion as a design principle. A values model deployed as a filter — sitting in a serving path, permitting or refusing — is defeated by publication of its weights, because the published artifact is precisely the oracle against which an attacker optimizes; a staged black-box attack (STACK) reaches roughly 71% success against a defended classifier pipeline that had held earlier attacks near zero, and an attacker holding the weights has strictly more than that attack needed. The same model published as an evaluator — emitting verdicts about systems it does not control — is not defeated by publication, and its positive findings are strengthened by it, because open weights are what allow a third party to reproduce and therefore to trust its verdicts. The same openness hands the judged party an optimization target, and §4.1 states what that concedes: a clean or empty result from an open referee proves less against an adaptive party than the first draft of this paper allowed. Openness is not a property with a fixed sign. Its sign is set by posture, and in the referee posture it is mixed. From this we derive a second result. The independent-evaluation literature documents at length the ways in which the evaluated party's control over access corrupts evaluation: short access windows, low rate limits, evaluator dependence on the goodwill and funding of the party being evaluated. We observe that the defect is symmetric and that, in the work surveyed in §2, its mirror image has not been named. An evaluator that controls access to its own judgments holds the same kind of power, pointed the other way — it can decline to evaluate, deprioritize, or be unavailable for a party it wishes to spare or to punish. We therefore specify a non-gatekeeping constraint : the ability to obtain a judgment must not depend on the evaluator's permission, which requires that the model, the harness, and the evaluation corpus be freely runnable, and which makes any hosted endpoint a convenience rather than a channel. We specify provenance-binding as the constitutive constraint on the model's outputs: every judgment must resolve to a citation into a fixed canonical corpus, and a judgment that cannot be so resolved is withheld rather than emitted. This trades coverage for auditability deliberately, and it distinguishes the artifact from values models trained on preference data whose sources cannot be named, and from purpose-authored value-rule corpora, whose rules are written for the alignment task itself and therefore cannot serve as an independent ground truth. Finally we specify that a single such artifact bears three non-interchangeable relations to the systems it judges, selected by carrier: a gate in the publisher's own hardware, a citation requirement without veto in an autonomous successor agent, and a referee in the wider world. We state plainly that the middle case must not be implemented as the first, because a veto held by a smaller model over a more capable agent bounds that agent at the evaluator's ceiling — the weak-supervisor problem applied to the very system the arrangement exists to enable. summary: PICSP3D is an open-source, three-dimensional, three-velocity (3D3V) electrostatic particle-in-cell code for plasma-object interaction, such as spacecraft and probe charging, sheaths and wakes, Langmuir probes, dust grains, electrodes, magnetised plasma devices and gas discharges. Objects of arbitrary shape are embedded in a uniform Cartesian grid as signed distance functions, built from analytic primitives with constructive solid geometry or imported from CAD (STL) with generalised winding numbers. The Poisson equation is solved with a multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradient method and second-order Shortley-Weller cut cells; floating and biased conductors are charged self-consistently through a capacitance matrix. The code includes surface processes (absorption, secondary electron emission, photoemission with self-shadowing), uniform and spatially varying static magnetic fields (dipoles, current loops, solenoids, mirrors, wires) with a Boris pusher, Monte Carlo collisions with a neutral background (elastic, charge exchange, excitation, ionisation) and binary Coulomb collisions. The solver is written in C++20 and parallelised with MPI domain decomposition and OpenMP threads; output is parallel VTK. A Python package, picsp_post, provides post-processing, figures, animations, Blender renders and a CAD import tool. The release contains the test suite, sixteen documented example cases with analysis scripts, the scaling benchmark and its results. Figures (in the repository): Logo ; CubeSat in low Earth orbit ; CubeSat ion wake ; protons trapped in a dipole field ; floating sphere and OML theory ; two-stream instability ; strong scaling on 72 cores . The full gallery and documentation are in the README .

summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. Every stage emits a machine-readable quality-control document, and later stages read those documents rather than trusting assumptions; provenance (input cube, SHA-256 hashes, specification version, wavelength frame, flux unit) travels with the products. Research code under active development. This is the version used in Ramírez Reyes & Cáceres (in preparation).

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. Two results on complementary (mutually unbiased) measurements and the complementary quantum correlation (CQC) inequality of Schneeloch, Broadbent and Howell (2014), which proposed that the classical correlations in two complementary measurement tables never exceed the quantum mutual information. 1. Sharp qutrit discrimination. For every pair of complementary bases of a qutrit and every two orthogonal states, the triangular discrimination summed over the two bases is at most 8/3 (the trivial ceiling is 4), answering Qian, arXiv:2608.14806v2, Section 11(4). Every equality case is classified; for the computational and Fourier bases they are tied to the nine Hesse SIC rays. Consequences: choosing one of the two measurements at random recovers at most two thirds of the quantum Fisher information in a two-state estimation task, and Qian's two-ray qubit-qutrit family obeys CQC with margin at least 0.1005 nats. Every prescribed pair fails for a qubit and a qudit of dimension n ≥ 4. For every prescribed pair of complementary measurements on each side there is a separable state violating CQC, with a uniform certified margin below −9/20,000,000 nats (previously the every-pair statement was known only for n ≥ 164). A phase-averaging extension of the known shared-label mechanism covers every prescribed pair when both dimensions are at least three; an earlier, unchecked every-pair statement for equal dimensions by E. O'Connor is credited. Open: the full qubit-qutrit CQC question and the sharp constant in dimension 5 (numerics only). The margins are tiny and structural, not experimental. summary: BarrierMap is a computational framework for comparing molecular permeability across the blood–brain barrier (BBB), skin, and intestinal Caco-2 systems. This record contains processed results, model summaries, cross-barrier analyses, and reproducibility materials supporting the associated manuscript. A common physicochemical descriptor baseline was combined with barrier-specific information, including ionization-derived descriptors for BBB and Caco-2 and anatomical/experimental context for skin. Predictive performance was evaluated using 20 repeated Bemis–Murcko scaffold-based train/test splits. Cross-barrier analyses were performed after molecular standardization using within-barrier percentile ranks to enable comparison among experimentally distinct permeability endpoints.
title: BarrierMap: Barrier-Specific Determinants of Molecular Permeability across Biological Interfaces

A common physicochemical descriptor baseline was combined with barrier-specific information, including ionization-derived descriptors for BBB and Caco-2 and anatomical/experimental context for skin. Predictive performance was evaluated using 20 repeated Bemis–Murcko scaffold-based train/test splits. Cross-barrier analyses were performed after molecular standardization using within-barrier percentile ranks to enable comparison among experimentally distinct permeability endpoints.
title: BarrierMap: Barrier-Specific Determinants of Molecular Permeability across Biological Interfaces

summary: This resource contains Python and Wolfram Mathematica variants of the simulation code accompanying the article Effect of Electoral Seat Bias on Political Polarization: A Computational Perspective by Daria Boratyn and Dariusz Stolicki ( International Journal of Public Opinion Research ). The code implements an agent-based Monte Carlo model designed to investigate how electoral seat bias in favor of larger parties affects the evolution of mass ideological polarization over repeated electoral cycles. The model represents voters and parties as ideal points in a two-dimensional policy space. Voter choice combines ideological proximity with preferences for larger parties, capturing strategic and bandwagon motives, and retrospective evaluations of government performance. Voter positions evolve through random preference perturbations, affective shifts associated with party attachment, and thermostatic responses to the incumbent. Electoral systems are represented by aggregate seats–votes functions: the pot-and-ladle approximation for Jefferson--D’Hondt and a power-law approximation for first-past-the-post plurality. The degree of seat bias is varied through mean district magnitude and the power-law exponent, respectively. Mass ideological polarization is measured using a modified Mehlhaff index with a degrees-of-freedom correction, with voter clusters identified through adaptive mean-shift clustering. The code is provided to facilitate inspection of the model’s assumptions and mechanisms, replication of the simulation experiments, and further computational research on the relationship between electoral institutions and political polarization.
title: Simulation Code for "Effect of Electoral Seat Bias on Political Polarization: A Computational Perspective"

summary: Operator Compounds: A Compositional Theory of Human Cognition and Behavior proposes a structural framework for understanding how elementary cognitive capacities combine to produce higher-order human capabilities. The theory introduces operators as functional cognitive capacities, operator compounds as stable organizations of interacting operators, and compound networks as higher-order organizations responsible for complex capacities such as deliberation, responsibility, self-regulation, resilience, and identity. The framework argues that development is fundamentally a process of organizational construction rather than information accumulation. Human capabilities emerge through the progressive formation, stabilization, and integration of operators, compounds, and networks. The paper develops a model of compound formation, degradation, collapse, and reconstruction, applies the framework to childhood development, proposes the Network Absorption Hypothesis, and outlines a research program with testable developmental predictions.
tags: operator theory; operator compounds; cognitive architecture; developmental psychology; child development; cognitive development; organizational complexity; self-organization; developmental systems; dynamic systems theory;
title: Operator Compounds: A Compositional Theory of Human Cognition and Behavior

summary: Revised manuscript with errata, and the CSV data behind the figures and tables of Xu (2024), On the statistical theory of self-gravitating collisionless dark matter flow: Scale and redshift variation of velocity and density distributions , Physics of Fluids 36, 117158, doi: 10.1063/5.0236964 , arXiv: 2202.06515 . Contents: the manuscript (P13_revised.pdf); statistics/ (53 CSV files, halo-based and correlation-based statistics); figures/ (32 CSV files, one per figure); tables.zip (19 CSV files); particles_velocity_pdfs.zip (13 particle and 15 velocity PDF CSV files). Companion datasets: Dataset Part I (halo-based), 10.5281/zenodo.6541231 ; Dataset Part II (correlation-based), 10.5281/zenodo.6757654 ; the 2022 preprint 10.5281/zenodo.6640676 ; and the slides 10.5281/zenodo.6569901 . Major findings (Virgo SCDM N-body simulation, ten redshifts): Delaunay tessellation reconstructs the comoving density field; the density correlation, spectrum and dispersion functions are obtained, modelled and compared with the N-body simulation. Velocity distributions are symmetric on small and large scales and non-symmetric with a negative skewness on intermediate scales, due to the inverse energy cascade at a constant rate ε u on small scales. On small scales, the even-order moments of the pairwise velocity Δu L follow a two-thirds law, ∝ (−ε u r) 2/3 , while the odd-order moments scale linearly, ⟨(Δu L ) 2n+1 ⟩ = (2n+1)⟨(Δu L ) 2n ⟩⟨Δu L ⟩ ∝ r. Fully developed velocity fields are never Gaussian on any scale, even when they start from a Gaussian initial condition. On small scales, u L and Σu L are modelled by an X distribution that maximises entropy; the distribution of Δu L can differ. On large scales, Δu L and Σu L are modelled by a logistic or an X distribution, while u L has a different distribution. The redshift variation of the velocity distributions follows the evolution of the X distribution, whose shape parameter α(z) decreases with time.
title: Dark matter flow data and manuscript: scale and redshift variation of velocity and density distributions

summary: VERSION 2 1. 𝓧 𝒇 sampling V2.0 covers a wider range of faradaic contributions, with faradaic up to 35%, distributed as follows: 𝓧 𝒇 = 0% (25% of CV curves) • 𝓧 𝒇 = 0–10% (50% of CV curves) • 𝓧 𝒇 = 10–35% (25% of CV curves) V1 was limited to 𝒳 𝑓 values between 0 and 10%, with very few purely capacitive CV curves (Xf = 0%). Predictions are valid for 𝒳 𝑓 ranging from 0% to 25%. Beyond 25%, the tool displays “Out of valid range”. 2. ESR and leakage messages When ESR or leakage contributions are negligible, the tool displays a message instead of a value: - “ESR contribution negligible” if 𝑹 𝒆𝒔𝒓 · 𝑰 𝒄 < 0.02 · ΔE (2% threshold vs. 1% in V1) - “Leakage contribution negligible” if 𝑰 𝒍𝒆𝒂𝒌 < 0.01 · 𝑰 𝒄 (1% of the capacitive current). 3. Capacitive–faradaic coupling V1. Only the capacitive current flowed through the ESR. The faradaic and leakage currents were computed at the applied potential E, so they caused no ohmic drop. V2. All currents flow through a common ESR, in series with three parallel branches: C, R leak , and the faradaic branch. Each value comes with a 95 % confidence interval computed for the analysed curve: value (low – high). A second neural network estimates the expected error for each curve and each parameter. A calibration step on 25,000 curves set aside from training (split conformal prediction) then sets the interval width so that it contains the true value for 95 % of the curves. On 50,000 test curves, coverage is 95.0 % (C), 95.1 % (R leak ), 94.9 % (ESR) and 95.2 % (𝒳 f ).
title: Physics-driven deep learning for inverse extraction of faradaic and capacitive parameters in supercapacitors: code, trained model and synthetic database

summary: Progress in robot learning, particularly physical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is currently challenged by a limited availability of accessible, standardized benchmarks. While simulation-based MARL has produced remarkable emergent behaviors, from coordinated team play to complex tool use, translating these advances to physical systems remains difficult. A key barrier is infrastructural: physical platforms are often prohibitively expensive, require specialized facilities, or lack open mechanisms and designs for reproducibility. We introduce KlaskTron, an open-source, low-cost (<\$2500 USD), desktop-scale robotic testbed for adversarial MARL based on the dynamic tabletop game KLASK. The platform features dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors, enabling the high-speed, precise manipulation required for competitive play. Crucially, we provide a complete ecosystem: hardware designs (CAD, BOM), a GPU-native digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Lab for high-fidelity modeling and simulation, and a validated sim-to-real baseline using a learned neural actuator model. We demonstrate that this baseline enables zero-shot policy transfer, with trained agents exhibiting emergent adversarial behaviors. To ensure full reproducibility of our results, all project assets are released publicly: hardware CAD/BOM and assembly documentation at [https://idscethzurich.github.io/klask_hardware], inference software stack at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_software] and the simulation and MARL setup at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_rl].
title: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL

summary: This repository presents an evidence-anchored, discipline-sensitive multicriteria assessment framework designed to support transparent, accountable, and reproducible evaluations of academic distinction and research integrity. The framework comprises a Microsoft Excel workbook organized into seven disciplinary classes corresponding to those of the European Academy of Sciences and Arts (EASA): 1. Humanities 2. Medicine 3. Arts 4. Natural Sciences 5. Social Sciences 6. Environmental and Technical Sciences 7. World Religions Each disciplinary class includes ten weighted assessment criteria evaluated on a five-level ordinal scale (0–4). Weighted scores are aggregated and normalized against the maximum attainable score for each class, generating percentage-based results and illustrative classification guidance. The workbook contains 15 worksheets, including discipline-specific evaluation forms, a scoring protocol, research integrity resources, an integrity register, a reusable audit template, and guidance for nominators. A central feature of the framework is the separation of academic merit assessment from research integrity verification. The integrity workflow supports the documentation and contextual examination of retractions, expressions of concern, citation irregularities, potential publication anomalies, and editorial or peer-review conflicts of interest. The framework distinguishes between unverified allegations, documented concerns, and substantiated findings. Bibliometric anomalies, retractions, or incomplete verification procedures must not automatically be interpreted as proof of individual research misconduct. The workbook also incorporates guidance for nominators regarding documentary evidence and the distinction between achievements that are not documented, criteria that have not yet been assessed, and verified absence of specific achievements. The assessment framework is intended to facilitate structured scholarly judgment rather than replace it. Its numerical weights and classification thresholds are illustrative methodological parameters and have not undergone independent empirical validation. Scope and limitations The instrument is proposed for academic discussion, methodological evaluation, pilot testing, and potential institutional adaptation. It is not an autonomous research misconduct detection system or a validated psychometric instrument. The workbook does not independently retrieve or verify bibliometric information. External sources require manual verification or separately implemented data-population procedures. The framework was independently developed with reference to the seven disciplinary classes of EASA. It does not constitute an officially adopted assessment policy of the European Academy of Sciences and Arts (EASA) or the World Academy of Art and Science (WAAS). Reproducibility and responsible use The accompanying README provides methodological information, scoring instructions, evidence requirements, research integrity safeguards, and limitations. Users are encouraged to document the evidence supporting individual scores, distinguish missing information from verified negative findings, and ensure independent review and appropriate procedural fairness before making consequential decisions. This Version 1.0 is provided as a transparent and reusable methodological resource for further examination, testing, and refinement. Keywords : Academic Evaluation; Research Integrity; Multicriteria Decision Analysis; Responsible Research Assessment; Evidence-Based Assessment; Bibliometrics; Academic Governance; Research Integrity Auditing; Academic Nominations; Scholarly Excellence.

summary: Manuscript and CSV data behind the figures and tables of Xu (2024), On the statistical theory of self-gravitating collisionless dark matter flow: High order kinematic and dynamic relations , Physics of Fluids 36, 075146, doi:10.1063/5.0215026 , arXiv:2202.02991 . Contents: the revised manuscript (PDF) and the CSV files of every plotted series and table, in the format of the author's dark matter flow datasets. Pair statistics from the Virgo SCDM N-body simulation at redshifts z = 10 to 0. Companion datasets: Part I (halo-based) doi:10.5281/zenodo.6541231 , Part II (correlation-based) doi:10.5281/zenodo.6757654 . Major findings (Virgo SCDM N-body simulation, redshifts z = 10 to 0): Kinematic relations of any order are derived for incompressible, constant-divergence and irrotational flow, and validated by the simulation. On large scales, third-order velocity correlations can be related to the density correlation or the pairwise velocity. The p-th order velocity correlations follow a^((p+2)/2) for odd p and a^(p/2) for even p (a = scale factor). The fitted exponents for odd p are smaller than these predictions. The overdensity is proportional to the density correlation on the same scale, <delta> ∝ <delta delta'>; the velocity dispersion on a scale r is proportional to the overdensity on that scale. The effective viscosity of the adhesion model originates from velocity fluctuations; the negative viscosity is due to the inverse energy cascade. On small scales, a self-closed velocity evolution is obtained by splitting velocity into motion within haloes and motion of haloes. Vorticity, enstrophy and energy evolution follow from it. The mean pairwise velocity follows <Δu_L> = −H a r. The third moment follows <(Δu_L)^3> ∝ ε_u a r, with a constant energy-cascade rate ε_u ≈ −4.6×10⁻⁷ m²/s³. The combined kinematic and dynamic relations give exponential velocity correlations on large scales and one-fourth power-law correlations on small scales; the p-th order correlations follow a^((3p−5)/4) for odd p and a^(3p/4) for even p.
title: Dark matter flow data and manuscript: On the statistical theory of self-gravitating collisionless dark matter flow: High order kinematic and dynamic relations

summary: This repository contains the code and numerical data supporting the manuscript “Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures” by Juan J. Segura. The study investigates how much relational information modular system interfaces must preserve in order to reconstruct an integrated dynamic-admissibility relation. The reproducibility package contains Python source code, benchmark configuration files, and CSV datasets and outputs used for the principal computational analyses. The package supports two complementary model layers: (1) a reduced continuous-control model used for exhaustive higher-order project-join analysis and robustness studies, and (2) a synthetic seven-state road-relative vehicle model used as a nonlinear dynamic falsification layer. The principal reproducible results include: complete pairwise reconstruction providing no improvement over unary reconstruction; persistence of this pairwise insufficiency across 27 combinations of numerical resolution, superelevation, and stopping horizon; and a sparse ternary architecture comprising the relations {R, mu, v}, {G, mu, v}, and {mu, v, tau} reproducing the complete third-order reconstruction in all 27 robustness cases. The vehicle parameters are synthetic and are not presented as OEM-calibrated haul-truck data. All admissibility projections are exact only with respect to the computed model relation. The reported discordance measures should not be interpreted as accident probabilities or empirical risk frequencies.
title: Code and Data for Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures

summary: Recovering a 3D full-body human bone rig, which is used to animate a Computer-Generated Image (CGI) model is a challenging problem with many applications although successfully addressed by the motion capture systems with actors with markers worn all over the body with special suit and multiple cameras . In this paper, we detail the bottom-up approach derived from Open Pose, winner of Common Objects in Context (COCO) 2016 KEYPOINTS Challenge, because of its decent qual ity and robustness of detection of multiple numbers of people in the frame with focus . Proposed network design and optimized post-processing with the full solution of video to 2D conversion run at acceptable speeds . The second part of 2D pose to 3D pose conversion u ses a novel Occlusion-Robust Pose-Maps (ORPM) which enables full body pose inference even under strong partial occlusions by other people and objects in the scene . O RPM outputs a fixed number of maps which encodes the 3D joint locations of all people in the scene . Body part associations allow us to infer 3D pose of arbitrary numbers of people without explicit bounding box prediction which increases performance of pose inference . The final combination of the two networks is where a single camera can detect human motion and display the 3D rep resentation in a three-dimensional space in real-time.  Provenance Note: Previously published in the Proceedings of the 3rd National Conference on Science, Engineering and Technology (SET Conference 2021) . Re-archived for public record due to the permanent closure of the original archive.
title: Motion Capture using POSENET

summary: Measured failure modes of verifier panels: companion paper accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? — Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels . Version of record: SSRN 7390698 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7390698 . Cite that version. The same text is also at https://polyhelper.ai/research/agreement-not-evidence/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/agreement-not-evidence . Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a non-expert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem: reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of "ten of them agreed." The protocol formalized here collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user's own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server. It reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich: the strongest available answer becomes the base, and each of the others contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it. Disagreements are kept in a section of their own rather than averaged away. The paper makes four contributions. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a merge can fail. Four of them are defects of naive pooling; the fifth is a failure of the operator rather than of the method: a synthesis that presents a single model's output as a collegial result. The second is the application of the correlated-witness arithmetic to protocol design. That arithmetic is not claimed here. Kohli (2026) applied the same Kish correction to a panel of nine frontier judges and measured about two effective votes, and Kim et al. (2025) established the underlying error correlation across more than 350 models. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Once a council is larger than 1/ρ, halving ρ beats doubling N, and a pair with low error correlation can outweigh five with high correlation. Which pairs those are is measured, not read off the label: the larger and more accurate models carry the most correlated errors even when architecture and provider differ (Kim et al., 2025), and the author's per-pair measurements found no detectable effect of geopolitical bloc on error correlation and, in the pairs measured, none of shared lineage (Chernets, 2026). The estimation procedure of Section 5.5 supplies that measurement. The third is an account of three deployment tiers, manual, one-tap mobile and browser-agent, and of the axis that separates them epistemically: whether the second model sees the first model's answer. Conditioning the second model raises ρ in exchange for error correction. The fourth is a small-sample observation of the counterfeit-council failure across five models, the one-sentence intervention that removed it in a three-model re-run, and a blinded three-arm evaluation design with a stated falsification condition. Correlated agreement is treated here as established, not as a finding. That a panel of models is worth far fewer independent witnesses than it has members has been measured directly: nine frontier judges drawn from seven families supply about two effective votes (Kohli, 2026), and error correlation rises with model capability even across providers and architectures (Kim et al., 2025). Section 5 restates the design-effect arithmetic behind those measurements, because three of the protocol's rules are derived from it and read as fastidiousness without it. The protocol then takes the other side of the same problem. That literature measures the correlation; this protocol

summary: A provenance-bound values model published as a public evaluator rather than deployed as a filter — why open weights defeat a filter and strengthen a referee, why the same weights bear three different relations to the model they judge, and why an evaluator that gatekeeps its own judgments has reproduced the defect it exists to correct. A values model — a model that judges conduct against a standard — is an established artifact. Guard models, safety classifiers, critic models, preference models and process reward models all instantiate the family, and the engineering is not in dispute. What is in dispute, and what this paper specifies, is the posture in which such an artifact is published , which we argue is not a deployment detail but the property that determines whether the artifact does anything at all. We state an inversion as a design principle. A values model deployed as a filter — sitting in a serving path, permitting or refusing — is defeated by publication of its weights, because the published artifact is precisely the oracle against which an attacker optimizes; a staged black-box attack (STACK) reaches roughly 71% success against a defended classifier pipeline that had held earlier attacks near zero, and an attacker holding the weights has strictly more than that attack needed. The same model published as an evaluator — emitting verdicts about systems it does not control — is not defeated by publication, and its positive findings are strengthened by it, because open weights are what allow a third party to reproduce and therefore to trust its verdicts. The same openness hands the judged party an optimization target, and §4.1 states what that concedes: a clean or empty result from an open referee proves less against an adaptive party than the first draft of this paper allowed. Openness is not a property with a fixed sign. Its sign is set by posture, and in the referee posture it is mixed. From this we derive a second result. The independent-evaluation literature documents at length the ways in which the evaluated party's control over access corrupts evaluation: short access windows, low rate limits, evaluator dependence on the goodwill and funding of the party being evaluated. We observe that the defect is symmetric and that, in the work surveyed in §2, its mirror image has not been named. An evaluator that controls access to its own judgments holds the same kind of power, pointed the other way — it can decline to evaluate, deprioritize, or be unavailable for a party it wishes to spare or to punish. We therefore specify a non-gatekeeping constraint : the ability to obtain a judgment must not depend on the evaluator's permission, which requires that the model, the harness, and the evaluation corpus be freely runnable, and which makes any hosted endpoint a convenience rather than a channel. We specify provenance-binding as the constitutive constraint on the model's outputs: every judgment must resolve to a citation into a fixed canonical corpus, and a judgment that cannot be so resolved is withheld rather than emitted. This trades coverage for auditability deliberately, and it distinguishes the artifact from values models trained on preference data whose sources cannot be named, and from purpose-authored value-rule corpora, whose rules are written for the alignment task itself and therefore cannot serve as an independent ground truth. Finally we specify that a single such artifact bears three non-interchangeable relations to the systems it judges, selected by carrier: a gate in the publisher's own hardware, a citation requirement without veto in an autonomous successor agent, and a referee in the wider world. We state plainly that the middle case must not be implemented as the first, because a veto held by a smaller model over a more capable agent bounds that agent at the evaluator's ceiling — the weak-supervisor problem applied to the very system the arrangement exists to enable. A consequence we did not initially see, an
title: The Referee, Not the Governor

summary: GEM Engine: Publication Dataset This dataset supports the research manuscript "GEM Engine: A reusable landscape-guided framework for exploration and optimization of genome-scale metabolic design spaces" by Hamed Rastaghi and Samuel M. D. Oliveira. GEM Engine is a computational framework designed to support reusable, landscape-guided exploration and optimization of genome-scale metabolic models. The framework combines flux balance analysis (FBA), surrogate modeling, and multi-objective optimization to enable systematic investigation of metabolic design spaces while reducing redundant simulations across optimization tasks. Dataset Contents Results.zip Contains genome-scale metabolic simulation landscapes, multi-objective optimization benchmarks, and associated computational results supporting the study. Figures_and_Tables.zip Contains data and materials associated with the main and supplementary figures and tables, including supporting analysis outputs and generation scripts where available. Reproducibility and Software The archived results support comparisons of landscape-guided optimization strategies, including gsMOBO, NSGA-II, SPARC, GHOST, and TRAIL, as well as surrogate-quality-based algorithm selection. The GEM Engine source code is maintained separately on GitHub. The repository URL will be provided when the software is publicly released.
title: GEM Engine: Simulation Landscapes and Optimization Benchmark Data for Genome-Scale Metabolic Design

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. In one sentence: identical Kuramoto oscillators scattered at random on a flat torus of any fixed dimension have stable twisted equilibria near every integer winding, which proves the twisted-equilibrium conjecture of Cirelli, Groisman, Huang and Vivas for every kernel in their class with |z|K(z) bounded. Place n identical oscillators at independent uniform points of the flat torus T d and couple points closer than ε n with weight K(z/ε n ). If ε n → 0 and nε n d+2 /log n → ∞, then with high probability, for every integer twist k with |k| ≤ c/(ε n +δ n ), where δ n = (log n/(nε n d+2 )) 1/2 , there is an asymptotically stable equilibrium whose phase differs from k·x by at most C|k|δ n at every vertex (Theorem 2.1). The kernel need only be even, supported in the unit ball, positive almost everywhere near the origin and have sup|z|K(z) finite: this covers the hard-radius graph, every bounded kernel and |z| −α , 0 < α ≤ 1. All twists k in Z d are covered, not only coordinate twists. Further results: at least c(ε n +δ n ) −d distinct stable constructed states; a basin of fixed size; for bounded radial kernels, a heat-equation limit uniform over all times; and stable weighted harmonic lifts under smooth nonuniform sampling (bounded kernels). The key tool is a sup-norm bound for the inverse graph Laplacian uniform over all conductances above a bounded backbone. The archive contains the manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source), an exact standard-library checker of classical cycle twisted-state spectra, the numerical illustrations with their script and records, verification and claim records, preserved development drafts, two unrelated supplementary research notes kept for provenance, a rating-free internal review summary, CI and SHA-256 sums. Assurance: written informal proofs; internal AI-agent review and proof audits only (not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification); kernels with |z|K unbounded and the connectivity regime nε d ~ log n remain open; constants are not explicit; the numerics are small illustrations outside the theorem's regime. Creator: Anonymous. Text and figures CC0-1.0; code MIT.
title: Stable twisted equilibria on random geometric tori in every fixed dimension

summary: A staged, reproducible pipeline for VLT/MUSE narrow-field-mode integral-field data: raw-cube reduction, spectral extraction of a faint companion next to a much brighter primary star with six independent extraction schemes, and hydrogen-line accretion analysis with detection limits calibrated against empirical nulls from control positions processed identically to the object. Every stage emits a machine-readable quality-control document, and later stages read those documents rather than trusting assumptions; provenance (input cube, SHA-256 hashes, specification version, wavelength frame, flux unit) travels with the products. Research code under active development. This is the version used in Ramírez Reyes & Cáceres (in preparation).
title: MUSE accretion pipeline

summary: BarrierMap is a computational framework for comparing molecular permeability across the blood–brain barrier (BBB), skin, and intestinal Caco-2 systems. This record contains processed results, model summaries, cross-barrier analyses, and reproducibility materials supporting the associated manuscript. A common physicochemical descriptor baseline was combined with barrier-specific information, including ionization-derived descriptors for BBB and Caco-2 and anatomical/experimental context for skin. Predictive performance was evaluated using 20 repeated Bemis–Murcko scaffold-based train/test splits. Cross-barrier analyses were performed after molecular standardization using within-barrier percentile ranks to enable comparison among experimentally distinct permeability endpoints.
title: BarrierMap: Barrier-Specific Determinants of Molecular Permeability across Biological Interfaces

summary: We describe our approach to the V2X-Real track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR from an Ouster OS1-64 unit, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism. Our final entry scores 0.7457 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.4382 and a realism score of 0.9251. Three findings account for most of our result, and all three were diagnostic rather than architectural. First, a coordinate frame mismatch between our predictions and the evaluation ground truth was suppressing detection AP entirely; recovering it took our score from 0.3520 to 0.5147 in a single submission. Second, a single global non maximum suppression threshold was destroying genuine pedestrian detections, because pedestrians occur in groups and a 0.3 IoU threshold applied to a 0.7 m box suppresses distinct neighbouring people; correcting this per class raised overall mAP from 0.0751 to 0.4295. Third, approximately 31 percent of the real reference point cloud consists of null returns encoded as the literal point (0, 0, 0), a format feature entirely absent from our synthetic clouds, which pinned Earth Mover's Distance near its floor until we modelled it. Negative results are reported at equal length, and Section 9 gives a full account of data provenance and compliance. That section also accounts for every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.
title: Coordinate Frame Recovery, Per Class NMS and Null Return Modelling for Sim2Real V2X LiDAR Detection

summary: We describe our approach to the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, in which a 3D object detector must be trained exclusively on synthetic data and evaluated on unseen real roadside LiDAR, while the synthetic point clouds are simultaneously scored for distributional realism. Our final entry scores 0.4793 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.1333 and a realism score of 0.9126. Our contribution is not a new architecture. Working from a PointPillars baseline, we obtained most of our gains from three sources. First, a diagnosis that small object failure in roadside LiDAR is a localisation problem rather than a detection problem, which led to a parameter free geometric refinement worth 86 percent relative on pedestrian AP. Second, an audit of our own post processing which revealed that a shipped rule was destroying valid predictions, the repair of which produced our single largest detection gain at 335 percent relative on the Van class. Third, treating the realism metrics analytically rather than as a black box, which showed that one of the four components is a closed form function of nine summary statistics. We also report an experimental methodology that we believe is the more transferable result. Because mean AP decomposes into independent per class terms, a single submission can carry several mutually controlled experiments, and a submission assembled entirely from previously measured components has a score that is known before it is sent. We predicted our final score to four decimal places prior to submission. We report negative results at equal length, and give a full account of data provenance and compliance in Section 8, including a full account of every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.

Our final entry scores 0.4793 combined, from a detection mAP of 0.1333 and a realism score of 0.9126. Our contribution is not a new architecture. Working from a PointPillars baseline, we obtained most of our gains from three sources. First, a diagnosis that small object failure in roadside LiDAR is a localisation problem rather than a detection problem, which led to a parameter free geometric refinement worth 86 percent relative on pedestrian AP. Second, an audit of our own post processing which revealed that a shipped rule was destroying valid predictions, the repair of which produced our single largest detection gain at 335 percent relative on the Van class. Third, treating the realism metrics analytically rather than as a black box, which showed that one of the four components is a closed form function of nine summary statistics. We also report an experimental methodology that we believe is the more transferable result. Because mean AP decomposes into independent per class terms, a single submission can carry several mutually controlled experiments, and a submission assembled entirely from previously measured components has a score that is known before it is sent. We predicted our final score to four decimal places prior to submission. We report negative results at equal length, and give a full account of data provenance and compliance in Section 8, including a full account of every mechanism contributing to the submitted score.
