summary: This article connects demographic renewal with multinational recruitment control and the operating life of committed capital. Its host-choice argument engages resource bundling and global staffing, with explicit conditions for shared recruitment, competition and border disruption. Version 3.65.0 adds a Bayesian decision analysis to the Nitra–Puebla staffing appraisal. Under the existing flat-margin, equal-offer-odds benchmark, choosing Nitra after losing the whole UK route carries an expected loss from choosing the wrong host of EUR0.14–1.00 million. Losing only intakes after year fourteen reduces that expected loss to about EUR2,000–15,000. Nitra retains the higher expected value in these reference comparisons. Appendix K11 derives the decision rule, reports alternative priors and provides two independent integrations of 312 specifications. These are conditional public-information appraisals before capital commitment, not realised JLR losses or evidence about its internal contracts. Existing Bayesian panel estimates, demographic inputs, propositions and eight figures are retained. The article distinguishes the measured population-access specification from the recruitment-control mechanism and explains common tenure through the timing of workforce replacement. No observations or regressions are added. Start with Main_Manuscript_ANONYMOUS.pdf, Online_Appendix_ANONYMOUS.pdf and README.txt. Compilable sources, public inputs, code, figure files and aggregate outputs are supplied. The current replication overlay and nine frozen base archives restore the complete permitted replication. Licensed WRDS rows require subscriber access; queries and reconstruction instructions are supplied. Editor-only cover and title pages are excluded.
title: Borrowed Youth: Demographic Change and Multinational Location Advantage — Article and Replication Materials

summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A Markov chain sampler estimates averages from one long trajectory; its accuracy is the long-run (asymptotic) variance of the time average. Adding a target-preserving rotation (a nonreversible perturbation) to overdamped Langevin samplers is known to help every observable. For kinetic (underdamped) Langevin samplers with friction γ, Duncan, Nüsken and Pavliotis (J. Stat. Phys. 2017) proved a local improvement for linear and quadratic observables of a Gaussian target when γ > √2 and conjectured it for every square-integrable observable. Results (exact stationary Gaussian dynamics, matched position and momentum rotations, position observables). (1) Every square-integrable observable's long-run variance never increases with rotation strength if and only if γ ≥ √2, endpoint included: a global form of the conjecture. The mechanism: the oscillator's power spectrum S(ξ) = 2γ/(ξ 4 + (γ 2 − 2)ξ 2 + 1) is single-peaked exactly when there is no resonance, rotation shifts the spectrum, and convolution keeps single peaks single. (2) The literal second-derivative form holds exactly on an explicit weighted Hermite class containing all polynomials; rough observables have sharper cusps. (3) Below the threshold, for every friction, even observables still improve at every rotation strength, only finitely many odd Hermite degrees can be hurt, and one finite rotation strength improves every observable. (4) Sharp large-rotation rates (uniform constant √(2π/e); slower for incommensurate rotation speeds). (5) For noncommuting stiffness K and friction Γ: ordering iff Γ 3 − ΓK − KΓ ≽ 0; the least safe friction (2K) 1/2 is a safety boundary, not an optimal friction; two coupled replicas make the criterion apply to any Gaussian target. (6) Fixed horizons and regular sampling can reverse the ordering; independent Poisson sampling preserves it. Scope. Gaussian targets only; no claim about numerical cost or discretised integrators (Duncan, Nüsken and Pavliotis found small friction best in practice). Classical ingredients (Breuer–Major Hermite identities, closure of symmetric unimodality under convolution, the convolution-power variance formula of Maini 2026) are credited, not claimed. Priority holds within a bounded literature search. Archive: manuscript (Markdown source, generated LaTeX and PDF), three deterministic verification scripts with their JSON reports, figure, extension notes, novelty reports, frozen targets, rating-free internal review record, bibliography with registry records, CI and SHA-256 manifests. Assurance: internal AI-assisted review only (not human peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification). Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
title: Sharp variance ordering for rotating Gaussian samplers

summary: Automatic tools can now generate whole-brain MRI parcellations at cohort scale, but generated-label releases often provide little evidence about which cases are reliable enough to reuse. We introduce OpenBrain, a confidence-aware release of 35,838 provenance-verified OpenNeuro T1w cases from 607 source datasets. OpenBrain is organized as an auditable case-record release rather than a directory of standalone segmentation files: each record links a primary parcellation, two committee parcellations, source/license provenance, raw QC-7 measurements, percentile risks, a combined risk score R, and a confidence tier. QC-7 is a reference-free reliability panel over label geometry, image-label consistency, and committee disagreement, so users can filter, weight, audit, or re-threshold generated labels without rerunning inference. We evaluate this released evidence under a frozen protocol. Across external cohorts, lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality; in fixed-budget training, lower-risk selections improve paired macro Dice over random selection by +3.2 to +3.7 percentage points. OpenBrain also exposes raw axes, committee outputs, provenance, and datasheet documentation, so confidence claims remain inspectable after download. It does not turn generated labels into manual annotations or clinical-grade segmentations. Its contribution is a large open generated-parcellation substrate, a reusable case-level risk-evidence layer, and an external validation protocol for release-time QC. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lanqz7766/OpenBrain. Code: https://github.com/lanqz7766/openbrain.
title: OpenBrain: An Auditable Generated-Label Release for Whole-Brain MRI Parcellation

summary: This paper presents a novel SAT encoding designed to represent a sequence of At-Most-K cardinality constraints arranged in a ladder-like structure, referred to as the Ladder AMK constraint. These AMK constraints feature a ladder-like arrangement, with shared common variables in the center and two variables differing at the beginning and the end. The proposed encoding first decomposes the sequence of AMK constraints into separated blocks, then encodes each block as a whole rather than encoding each AMK constraint individually. This approach improves the efficiency of constraint solving in SAT solvers by significantly reducing the size of the encoding, precisely the number of variables, and the generated clauses required. To achieve this, the encoding employs Sequential Counter to encode each block and constructs clauses that link adjacent blocks, ensuring equivalence with the input constraints. Compared to the previously proposed encoding that uses BDD for Ladder AMO constraint, our encoding requires fewer variables and clauses. Our study is the first study that develops SAT encoding for Ladder AMK constraints with k>1. Experimental results on single Ladder AMO and Ladder AMK constraints indicate that our encoding significantly enhances both the size of the encoding and the efficiency of solving time compared to existing encodings. Furthermore, by evaluating on the two real-world combinatorial problems, namely Anti-bandwidth Problem and Nurse Rostering Problem, we found that the proposed encoding surpasses alternative encodings, as well as more advanced Constraint Programming and Mixed Integer Programming solvers. In summary, the SAT encoding technique presented in this paper provides a more efficient method for encoding sequence constraint, specifically Ladder AMK constraint, which could enhance the effectiveness of SAT solving for various problems involving this type of constraint.
title: SAT Encoding for Set of At-Most-K Cardinality Constraints with Ladder Shape

summary: This paper presents a novel SAT encoding designed to represent a sequence of At-Most-K cardinality constraints arranged in a ladder-like structure, referred to as the Ladder AMK constraint. These AMK constraints feature a ladder-like arrangement, with shared common variables in the center and two variables differing at the beginning and the end. This approach improves the efficiency of constraint solving in SAT solvers by significantly reducing the size of the encoding, precisely the number of variables, and the generated clauses required. summary: Between 2010 and 2023, Niger faced escalating security and governance crises that culminated in the military coup of 26 July 2023. Conventional accounts often describe this trajectory in terms of state fragility, treating institutional weakness primarily as a deficit requiring technical reform. This article instead critically examines the explanatory value of Frantz Fanon's theory of postcolonial crisis in The Wretched of the Earth. Drawing on historical scholarship, empirical studies and policy reports, it develops five propositions concerning the inherited colonial state, the intermediary national bourgeoisie, the political marginalisation of the masses, neocolonial dependence, and the failure to transform national consciousness into social consciousness. Each proposition is assessed against developments in Niger between 2010 and 2023. The analysis finds that Fanon offers particular insight into elite intermediation, unequal access to state resources and externally mediated political power. Nevertheless, his framework gives insufficient attention to the relative autonomy of customary and religious authorities, transnational armed organisations and contemporary security partnerships. The 2023 coup further complicates his account by showing how military actors can appropriate the language of national liberation without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to social transformation. The article argues that Fanon's work remains valuable as a critical diagnosis of historically produced political relations, but should not be treated as a deterministic explanation of Niger's institutional trajectory.

summary: Code, derived data and result files for Differentiable Neuro-Fuzzy Reasoning (DNFR), a path-based link predictor that learns degree-aware edge memberships, a Schweizer–Sklar t-norm per metapath and metapath reliabilities, and aggregates paths by noisy-OR, used as an instrument for a controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs. Tasks: drug repurposing in Hetionet v1.0 and PrimeKG, disease–symptom prediction in Hetionet and in the graded health knowledge graph of Rotmensch et al. (2017), and a secondary test on a NHANES fuzzy relation, under leave-dyad-out random and disease-centred splits. Comparators: fixed t-norms, component ablations, restarts of the t-norm parameter, DWPC with logistic regression (with and without degree and prior features), a degree-preserving edge prior, popularity, AnyBURL, truncated and soft-thresholded SVD and knowledge graph embeddings. Version v3.0-rev3 (third revision) adds DNFR 2.0, four refinements tested one at a time and in combination (overlap-aware aggregation, Gumbel-softmax operator choice, an information-content hub discount and membership annealing), a fixed t-norm selected on validation data, a converged L-BFGS profile of the t-norm parameter, an unbounded parameterisation, a compact NBFNet baseline, an exact edge-level Shapley attribution of the explanations, a mechanistic classification of the drug-repurposing explanations, a sparsity variant that keeps the target relation, and 10 leave-dyad-out splits for the main comparisons on Hetionet compound–treats–disease, Hetionet disease–symptom and the graded health knowledge graph. Version 1.1.0 (second revision) added a profile analysis of the t-norm parameter, training without early stopping, additional splits, equivalence tests, the edge prior, share-matched and edge-level explanation tests, unit tests and the script that builds the manuscript from the statistics files. Includes per-query ranks for every method and split, trained models, path explanations, and the statistics files from which every number in the manuscript is read. Hetionet and PrimeKG are downloaded by download_data.py with MD5 checks.

summary: This dataset contains the raw and processed experimental data associated with the study "Eco-Friendly and Large-Scale Fabrication of Microelectronic Silk-Based Enzymatic Biosensors". The collection includes measurements related to silk fibroin film fabrication and characterization, electron-beam lithography process optimization, nanostructure dimensional analysis, and enzymatic activity assays of horseradish peroxidase immobilized within silk fibroin matrices. Raw instrument outputs, processed datasets, statistical analyses, and metadata describing experimental conditions are provided to ensure transparency and reproducibility. The dataset supports the development of environmentally friendly microfabrication strategies for enzyme-based bioelectronic devices and may be reused for studies involving silk fibroin processing, enzyme immobilization, biopolymer lithography, and microelectronic biosensor fabrication

summary: SimilCode Benchmark is a controlled dataset of 120 source-code pairs in C# and Java (15 reference programs per language, four similarity categories: identical, functional, structural and different) for evaluating source-code similarity detectors in programming education. It includes the raw results of a replicated evaluation of four commercial large language models (GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4-pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5; 1,440 evaluations, three replicas per pair and model) and the outputs of Moss, JPlag and Dolos on the same pairs; a classification of the pairs by code-clone type; a second run with 84 copies of the reference programs rewritten with generative AI (by a local open-weight model and by commercial models), verified by execution and scored together with independent solutions to the same exercises (1,368 LLM evaluations and the three detectors), including the refusals of the generators; an analysis of how well each dimensional score of the language models, their weighted global score and a derivation score that excludes functional similarity separate copies from independent solutions; the validation corpus and predictions of the Big O estimator of SimilCode; and scripts that reproduce the reported numbers without calling any API. Contents, protocol and reproduction instructions: see README.md, CHANGELOG.md and copias_ia/README_COPIAS_IA.md in the archived repository.
title: SimilCode Benchmark: A Dual-Language Source-Code Similarity Dataset for the Evaluation of AI-Based Detectors

summary: Saigon300 is a semi-synthetic benchmark for the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Version 1.0.0 archives 56 instances with 300 customers and one depot each: C1 (9), C2 (8), R1 (12), R2 (11), RC1 (8), and RC2 (8). The package contains eight shared asymmetric OSRM distance/duration matrices, instance files, BIH verification and OR-Tools code, figures, and recorded experimental outputs. Matrix units are metres and seconds; the routing profile is car. Source metadata reports an OpenStreetMap snapshot dated 2026-05-26. This deposit is an unchanged snapshot of public repository commit 555ac7d2eb9d2af402bdb23f9633e3af435d8ab4: https://github.com/ltlong-SGU/Saigon300-VRPTW . ZIP integrity and node IDs 0..300 for all 56 instance files have been checked. This is not a new solver experiment or full independent replication. Authors: Le Tan Long and Phan Tan Quoc (Saigon University); Do Phan Thuan (Ho Chi Minh City University of Industry and Trade), as stated in the source metadata. Original source licences are retained: CC BY 4.0 for the dataset; source metadata separately declares MIT for code. Upstream rights remain applicable to OpenStreetMap/OSRM-derived components; OpenStreetMap attribution: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright . This dataset deposit is separate from the accepted Saigon300 camera-ready paper, which is not included.

summary: Documentation release, results unchanged. ERA5-Land is no longer presented as a baseline: the model uses WorldClim and ERA5 (1991-2020) with Climate Digital Twin changes, which already agree against the null control. A new README section describes future work on daily indices (frost days, hot days, dry spells, length of the warm season) from daily data; the ERA5-Land download scripts and the era5land Snakemake step are kept for that work and labelled as not part of the results. Draft, open to correction by the authors of the original work.

Draft, open to correction by the authors of the original work.

summary: Abstract Water balance penalties may improve numerical closure while reallocating error among unobserved ‎fluxes. We investigate this compensation and the limits of selecting a penalty for annual flood ‎prediction. Forty-five trained synthetic LSTMs isolate forcing, exchange, and initialization ‎disturbances. Thirty-five matched regional models and five accounting references use 89 quality-quality-‎screened CAMELS-AUS catchments, partitioned into 54 for development, 15 for selector validation, ‎and 20 for confirmation. Under 40% precipitation underestimation, fixed and bounded penalties ‎reduce estimated evapotranspiration below 1% of generating truth in all eight held-out synthetic ‎catchments. A historically selected rule lowers confirmation-normalized annual-maximum error ‎from 2.29 to 2.21, a 3.54% point reduction. The original conditional interval barely excludes zero, ‎and river-region sign randomization gives p = 0.0625. A post hoc 100,000-draw analysis retains a ‎near-zero upper endpoint, with numerical sub-batches still reaching or crossing zero. Direct paired ‎comparisons with simpler alternatives all span zero; the selector does not establish added predictive ‎value. Its seven active catchments occupy only five regions. Recovery of the original final archive ‎verifies the selection lock, completed fit records, and hashes of all 40 real/reference prediction files. ‎These findings support a controlled latent-compensation mechanism and a reproducible limitation ‎of selective regularization, while leaving real-catchment process attribution and robust predictive ‎superiority unresolved. ‎ Keywords: rainfall-runoff modeling; water balance; annual flood maxima; model misspecification; ‎spatial transfer; uncertainty
title: Ayad-Kathim-Hussein/Prof.-Dr.-Ayad-K.-H.-Alkhafaji: Why selective mass penalties do not reliably improve annual flood maxima: An 89-‎catchment diagnostic with recovered provenance
